newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries quietly firmer in late Tokyo trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries quietly firmer in late Tokyo trade.

text.p: The price of the key U.S. Treasury long bond was a tad firmer in quiet late Tokyo trade on Tuesday in reaction to limited position adjustments by traders.
Investors were sidelined ahead of Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony before the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday.
Participants are wary because Greenspan may say something to check the rise of buoyant U.S. stocks.
"If the (U.S.) stock market were to tumble, this would also be bearish for bonds and the dollar, causing triple weakness in the U.S. financial markets," said a U.S. brokerage trader.
